result.title: AI Brain Fry Is Real. Here’s What Leaders Can Do | Julie Bedard | TED
result.description:
Workers everywhere are quietly redesigning their jobs around AI, boosting productivity but also creating new kinds of problems. AI advisor Julie Bedard thinks she has a fix. She shares new research on three areas for leaders to focus on — including how to avoid "AI brain fry" — and why we need to shape this change rather than let it happen to us. (Recorded at TED@BCG on August 17, 2026)

result.description:

In this actionable talk, she explains how to make sure you're showing your true potential at work and beyond. (Recorded at TEDxUofW on April 19, 2026)

result.title: In a world of endless health advice, clarity and context might be the best prescription #TEDTalks
result.description: Why does searching your symptoms online always leave you more frightened than before? As former chief medical officer of WebMD, physician John Whyte spent years believing more information meant better health — until he saw how too much of it was making people spiral. In a world of health influencers, algorithms and AI tools designed to keep you clicking, he reveals why clarity and context is a better prescription.

result.title: I Can’t Speak. Here’s How I Get People to Listen | Jessica Irwin | TED
result.description:
Jessica Irwin is many things: a photographer, artist, author, performer. She also happens to be nonverbal, born with cerebral palsy that affects the muscles she needs to talk. Speaking through a device that turns her typed words into speech, she gives a sharp, funny and urgent reminder that being unable to speak has nothing to do with intelligence — and shares a few easy ways anyone can better communicate with nonverbal people. (Recorded at TED2026 on April 16, 2026)
